[u][b]Summary if you don’t want to read the whole review:[/b][/u] the game is very fun, but I ultimately felt that nostalgia plays a big factor in why many people would claim this is the greatest adventure game of all time. Really fun, but not as special as I was hoping it would be.

This is a very interesting game. I’m surprised at how popular this game is, since I’m not from Germany or from the USA, so knowing it was popular definitely elevated my expectations about how good this game could be. I don’t think that creating expectations is inherently a bad thing, but it definitely made me play it with sharper critical lenses than I would’ve put on a game that was originally released in 1993. 

[u][b]So let’s start with the positives.[/b][/u]

[b]+[/b] The game oozes with charm. From the surrealist aesthetics of the scenery to the carefully animated characters based on Chuck Jones’ - Looney Tunes - style of animation, with really exaggerated stretch and squash that makes things look like they’re some sort of play-dough. The music from this game also rocks, both the original and the remastered - I couldn’t decide which one I wanted to keep playing with, since both sounded so good.

[b]+[/b] The narrative is really creative and it had some really funny jokes, and it impressed me that most of the jokes wouldn’t be problematic today - which is something that is kind of a recurring theme for older adventure games. Not that I care that much about it, but it definitely impressed me how well the creative elements of this game really stood the test of time in many shapes and forms.

[b]+[/b] From the moment I started playing, I couldn’t put the game down. It was intriguing and fun trying to find out what would be the next piece of the puzzle, or try to find out what I was missing. It really was a magnetic experience in that regard. Having three completely different sets of interactable scenes made this game’s puzzles be a blast, and considering what changes to the future each interaction would bring was a really fun way to keep players thinking about puzzles that they weren’t doing at the moment.

[b]+[/b] Lastly, I also LOVE that you can choose how to play the game as it was back then, as the remaster, or mix’n’match the settings. Being able to change it with just a hotkey was also a very nice touch. Still along these lines, being able to play the original Maniac Mansion (the prequel of Day of the Tentacle) from inside the game was also marvelous, but I wish there was an option to do so from the menu. I’m glad I have played Maniac Mansion and it made me appreciate DotT much more than I would’ve otherwise.

[u][b]Now, for the negatives.[/b][/u] First, I’ll talk about things that should’ve been in the remaster, and then about things I didn't like about the original game.

[b]-[/b] There’s no hint system in this game. I understand how hints can actually discourage people from thinking, but in a game that has many moments of moon logic, I feel like that should’ve been mandatory to at least have some small directions. I say that as someone who couldn’t get many of the hints based on history, as I’m not too versed in North American colonial history, so something to help out in terms of direct gameplay impact would definitely help.

[b]-[/b] Why on earth are there verbs that make no sense for some objects? The showing of the verbs is extremely inconsistent throughout the game, and showing irrational verbs made me completely ignore some of them and get stuck in puzzles that were supposed to be easy otherwise. For example, why is there an option to “open/close” or “pull/push” a coin in the inventory? Don’t get me wrong, I do think that verbs that have no action - BUT MAKE SENSE - should appear in the dial, but putting them in places where they made no sense made it so I just started to ignore some of the verbs altogether.

[b]-[/b] Now, dislikes about the game itself. Most characters have very interesting personalities, especially the playable ones, but I really wish that the three main characters had some skill or uniqueness in gameplay for each. They’re just differently colored shells with the same filling in each. I didn’t feel like it mattered what each character was for the period they were in. I feel like the same applies to items, because each item had a specific purpose in the game and other solutions for puzzles didn’t apply - even logical ones. There are many more ways to remove a sticky gum from the floor than the singular way that the game mandatorily makes you do.

[b]-[/b] And at last, some minor complaints. It was way too inconsistent to be able to know from a glance which items were able to be sent across time - some big ones couldn’t, but then some other big ones could, and that made it so weird and arbitrary. I also think that the conversation system could’ve used some polish, as I couldn’t understand if I was having a singular conversation with unique answers that wouldn’t come back, or if I was in a multi-choice answer phase.

[u][b]The bottom line.[/b][/u]

This game was really fun and it captivated and entertained me with its fun visuals, narrative, music and clever puzzles, but I feel like the remaster itself could’ve improved a lot more than it did, especially because there was an option to toggle between the remaster and the original versions, so there’s no reason not to try to improve the gameplay a little more. Still, it was really fun, but it didn’t meet my expectations.

Day of the Tentacle Remastered é simplesmente um clássico que todo fã de point and click deveria jogar.

Para quem já conhece o gênero, esse jogo dispensa apresentações. Com um visual cartunesco incrível e um humor muito marcante, ele consegue ser divertido do início ao fim. Além disso, para quem jogou Maniac Mansion, a experiência fica ainda melhor, já que o jogo funciona como uma espécie de continuação e traz várias referências ao título anterior.

A jogabilidade segue o clássico estilo point and click: pegar itens, conversar com personagens, resolver puzzles e encontrar soluções criativas para avançar na história. Tudo funciona muito bem, e os desafios são divertidos sem se tornarem cansativos.

O trabalho feito no remaster ficou excelente. Os gráficos foram atualizados com muito cuidado, mantendo totalmente a essência do original. O jogo continua com o mesmo charme, só que com uma qualidade visual muito melhor.

A história também é um grande destaque. Controlar Bernard, Hoagie e Laverne em uma aventura cheia de situações engraçadas e momentos memoráveis torna a experiência ainda mais especial. Sem spoilers, mas quem conhece Maniac Mansion vai se sentir em casa.

E um detalhe que deixa tudo ainda melhor: o próprio Maniac Mansion está completo dentro do jogo, o que por si só já agrega muito valor.

No fim das contas, é um jogo que vale cada centavo e que recomendo muito, tanto para fãs do gênero quanto para quem quer conhecer um dos grandes clássicos dos videogames.

Day of the Tentacle Remastered es una auténtica joya del género de aventuras gráficas, una experiencia que demuestra que los grandes juegos nunca pasan de moda. Con su humor irreverente, personajes memorables y situaciones absurdamente creativas, logra enganchar desde el primer momento.

La historia, centrada en viajes en el tiempo y en evitar que un tentáculo malvado conquiste el mundo, es tan original como divertida. En resumen, Day of the Tentacle Remastered es una combinación perfecta de humor, creatividad y nostalgia. Un título imprescindible que no solo celebra el pasado de los videojuegos, sino que demuestra por qué sigue siendo uno de los mejores exponentes del género.

🧪 Day of the Tentacle Remastered - Zeitreise, Humor & Point-and-Click-Kult.
„Day of the Tentacle Remastered“ ist die modernisierte Version des klassischen Adventure-Spiels von LucasArts aus den 90ern. In der skurrilen Geschichte versuchen drei sehr unterschiedliche Charaktere, eine Weltübernahme durch mutierte Tentakel zu verhindern. Durch ein fehlgeschlagenes Experiment werden sie allerdings versehentlich in verschiedene Zeitperioden geschickt - Vergangenheit, Gegenwart und Zukunft. Um die Katastrophe zu stoppen, muss man clever zwischen den Zeiten wechseln und Rätsel lösen, die oft mehrere Epochen miteinander verbinden.

🎮 Gameplay:
Klassisches Point-and-Click mit cleveren Zeitreise-Rätseln. Man steuert drei Figuren, die jeweils in einer anderen Zeitlinie gefangen sind. Viele Rätsel funktionieren nur, wenn man Gegenstände durch die Zeit schickt oder Ereignisse in einer Epoche verändert, damit sie in einer anderen Auswirkungen haben. Das sorgt für kreative Puzzle-Ideen und einige echte „Aha“-Momente. Die Steuerung wurde für die Remastered-Version modernisiert, bleibt aber dem klassischen Adventure-Prinzip treu.

🎬 Story & Charaktere:
Abgedreht, humorvoll und voller Charme. Die Geschichte ist bewusst übertrieben und lebt von ihrem absurden Humor. Charaktere wie Bernard, Hoagie und Laverne sind herrlich unterschiedlich und sorgen für viele lustige Dialoge. Besonders die Begegnungen mit historischen Figuren - etwa George Washington oder Benjamin Franklin - gehören zu den Highlights. Das Spiel nimmt sich selbst nie zu ernst und bleibt bis zum Ende unterhaltsam.

🎨 Atmosphäre & Präsentation:
Bunt, cartoonhaft und zeitlos. Die Remastered-Version bietet komplett überarbeitete handgezeichnete Grafiken, die den Stil des Originals respektieren, aber deutlich schärfer wirken. Die Animationen sind lebendig und passen perfekt zum humorvollen Ton des Spiels. Besonders schön: Man kann jederzeit zwischen der neuen und der klassischen Grafik wechseln.

🔊 Musik & Sounddesign:
Verspielt und passend zum Humor. Die Musik unterstützt die verrückte Stimmung hervorragend und bleibt angenehm im Hintergrund. Die englische Sprachausgabe ist hervorragend umgesetzt und bringt die vielen humorvollen Dialoge perfekt zur Geltung. Auch Soundeffekte und kleine akustische Details sorgen für zusätzlichen Charme.

👥 Wiederspielwert:
Begrenzt, aber nostalgisch reizvoll. Die Geschichte verläuft linear, weshalb der Wiederspielwert eher gering ist. Allerdings macht es Spaß, das Spiel später noch einmal zu starten - besonders um Dialoge, Gags oder alternative Lösungswege für Rätsel zu entdecken.

🔍 Technik:
Saubere Remaster-Umsetzung. „Day of the Tentacle Remastered“ läuft stabil und bietet einige Komfortfunktionen wie moderne Steuerung, Kommentarspuren der Entwickler und die Möglichkeit, jederzeit zwischen alter und neuer Grafik zu wechseln. Kleine Komfortverbesserungen machen das Spiel zugänglicher, ohne den klassischen Adventure-Charme zu verlieren.

✅ Fazit:
„Day of the Tentacle Remastered“ ist ein hervorragendes Beispiel dafür, wie man ein klassisches Adventure modernisiert, ohne seinen ursprünglichen Charme zu verlieren. Kreative Zeitreise-Rätsel, herrlich absurder Humor und liebevoll überarbeitete Grafik machen das Spiel auch heute noch zu einem der besten Point-and-Click-Adventures.

👍 Empfohlen für:
Fans klassischer Point-and-Click-Adventures
Spieler*innen mit Sinn für absurden Humor
Menschen, die kreative Rätsel und charmante Storys mögen

👎 Nicht empfohlen für:
Spieler*innen, die schnelle Action oder moderne Gameplay-Systeme erwarten
Fans sehr kurzer oder sehr linearer Spiele ohne Rätsel
Menschen, die mit klassischem Adventure-Gameplay wenig anfangen können

🌟 Endbewertung: 9/10 - Sehr positiv

Day of the Tentacle was originally released in 1993 and to me is one of the classic point and click puzzle games. This is one of the games that shaped my early gamer years and so it was a really heartwarming experience to replay, now I finally have access to a platform that can play it (bought a Steam Deck).

The remaster does an incredible job of modernising the graphics in a way that felt like that’s what they always must have looked like. You can switch back to the original graphics and audio on the fly with a click of a button, and I couldn’t believe that’s what I originally played! The game played great and I’d highly recommend it to anyone with either a sense of humour or an appreciation of light hearted story/puzzle games.

I played with the developer commentary on and it was just wonderful to hear a Tim Schafer and the original developers break down how they built the game, and the amusing limitations and decisions they faced back in the day when games were sold on floppy disks.

The game itself is a classic point and click. By that I mean you control a character who can interact with stuff on screen, and you have to collect, use and combine items with other things to solve puzzles. In DOTT, you can switch between three characters, each stuck in a different period of time at the same location, and use a few ways of passing items to each other to solve your respective goals.

The voice acting is amazing, the script is really funny, the plot is unique (pet tentacle grows arms and takes over the world) and somehow this deeply engaging puzzle game takes place within a single house.

Highly recommended 💯

My favourite ever point n' click adventure, played near original release (on a friends PC) and managed to finish it without using any guides or getting overly-stuck. Twenty odd years later and the game is every bit as good as it was back then. It was so memorable I even remembered some of the solutions from all those years ago.

The remaster itself is also good, You can switch (with a button press) between the classic or remastered versions. 

The classic version retains the beautiful pixel art of old but you don't get much screen for the actual game, big borders to the sides and the UI takes up the bottom third. Also you can't use the new control scheme which is much better if you play with a controller.

The remaster uses the entire screen for gameplay and is much better if you play with a controller but honestly (personnal taste thing) I didn't like the re-traced, smoothed out graphics. Luckily you can use Reshade with YeetronCRT filter to make the game look absolutely stunning, like high definition pixel art.

This is one of the games from the 'golden era' of LucasArts titles, which were all classics - Maniac Mansion, Monkey Island, Full Throttle, The Dig, to name but a few, and despite it's age, its still a thoroughly enjoyable experience.  The remastered graphics and sound are great and game is genuinely really funny; it has a lot of character to it.  Try and play without the walkthrough unless you get really stuck, its the most enjoyable way!  Maniac Mansion actually comes free inside this game also, as an optional side quest, which is cool all in itself.
